Department: Enterprise Engineering - Smart Switch Software Development
Employment Type: Full-time

About NETGEAR

NETGEAR has been pioneering advanced networking technology since 1996, delivering innovative products that connect people to the internet, power businesses, and enable digital experiences. Our Smart Switch product line serves small-to-medium businesses and enterprises worldwide, offering advanced L2/L3 managed switching with cloud-based management through NETGEAR Insight. About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Engineer I to join our Smart Switch firmware team in Chennai. You will be a technical anchor for the team - designing, developing, and maintaining embedded Linux firmware for NETGEAR's smart switch product families spanning 20+ SKUs across multiple hardware platforms.

This role sits at the intersection of hardware and software: you will work with switch ASIC SDKs, implement and optimize L2/L3 networking protocols, develop kernel modules, and ensure production-quality firmware for ARM64/MIPS-based networking devices. You will collaborate daily with the various engineering teams and have significant ownership over critical platform subsystems.

As the industry shifts toward agentic engineering - where engineers orchestrate AI coding agents to handle implementation while focusing their own expertise on architecture, system design, and validation - we expect this role to embrace AI-augmented workflows as a core part of daily development.

This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives on solving deep technical problems in embedded networking systems and leverages AI tools to amplify their productivity.

- Stacking & Distributed Systems: Contribute to the multi-unit stacking feature set - topology management, member election, cross-unit configuration synchronization, firmware upgrade coordination, and hot-swap support.

- Cross-Platform Delivery: Develop and maintain firmware across multiple product families (ARM64 and MIPS architectures), coordinating changes across shared codebases to ensure consistency.

- Code Quality & Reviews: Conduct thorough code reviews, define coding standards for the team, and champion best practices in embedded C development. Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, memory leaks, and race conditions.

- Collaboration: Work closely with the various engineering teams across time zones. Participate in architecture discussions, design reviews, and release planning. Mentor junior engineers on the Chennai team.

- Build & Release: Maintain and improve the cross-compilation build system (GNU Make, Docker). Support release engineering processes including image generation, debug builds, and OSS compliance (SBOM).

Guide the team in adopting agentic engineering practices where AI agents handle routine implementation tasks while you focus on architecture, validation, and system-level thinking.

We're looking for native-level English (AU) speakers with professional voice recording experience to join the Hydrus Project.

Audition with two 30 second samples using your home studio set up

Participate in natural conversation, prompted discussion, and scripted customer-service scenarios
Record from your own home studio setup across both sessions
Your Recording Environment
Three things are required, and each is judged separately:
An external microphone: A separate, dedicated microphone is absolutely required - see below.
A dry room: Your voice should sound close and clear, with no echo or hollow, distant quality. Untreated rooms with bare walls, hard floors, and high ceilings usually fail. 
A quiet room: No HVAC hum, fans, traffic, appliances, or household noise during recording.
Minimum Required Gear
Dynamic Mics (best for untreated rooms): Shure SM58, Shure MV7 / MV7+, RODE PodMic / PodMic USB, or similar.
Condenser mic (great in a treated room): RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti / Yeti Orb, Blue Bluebird, Blue Baby Bottle, or similar.
Room Treatment: Your recording space should produce studio-quality sound samples - isolation shields, sounds absorbing pads, etc… 
Immediately rejected: built-in laptop microphones, phone mics, AirPods, Samsung Buds, headphone-attached mics, headsets, and gaming headsets.

WAV format, 24-bit, 48 kHz, no compression. Free software such as Audacity can produce this. If you cannot export in this format, please do not apply - this level of technicality is required for this role.

A dry, quiet home recording space and a professional microphone, as described above
